blocks.text: You can add VPN diagnostic sessions that run commands on VPN Service Edges, Network Connectors, and Network Connector groups. You can then filter and view the outputs of these sessions to assist in troubleshooting.
VPN diagnostics are supported on VPN Service Edge and Network Connector version 26.46.3 and later.
To add a VPN diagnostic session:

blocks.item: Go to Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > VPN Support Information.
Click Add.

blocks.text: The Add VPN Session drawer appears.

blocks.item: In the Add VPN Session drawer:
Name: Enter the name of the diagnostic session.
VPN Service Edges: Select the VPN Service Edges that the data is collected from.
Network Connectors: Select the Network Connectors that the data is collected from.
Network Connector Groups: Select the Network Connector groups that the data is collected from.
Commands: Select the command for the VPN diagnostic session.
Session Commands
The following table provides a list of commands available for a VPN diagnostic session:

table: The DNS lookup command to resolve the AAAA record. Ports are not specified in DNS lookup commands.
The DNS lookup command to resolve the A record. Ports are not specified in DNS lookup commands.
The DNS lookup command to resolve the SRV record. Ports are not specified in DNS lookup commands.

The crypto ping command verifies connectivity between your VPN Service Edge and one or more Network Connector. This command is exclusive and cannot be run with other commands. This command can only be run from a VPN Service Edge.
Not applicable. The Targets field changes to NP Target Connector. Select the destination Network Connector.
The Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) ping command to test reachability of a host on an Internet Protocol (IP) network.
Examples of valid arguments: jira.corp.com 1.1.1.1 google.com
The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) ping command to test reachability to a port, or range of ports, for a list of hostnames or IP addresses.
Examples of valid arguments: jira.corp.com:80 1.1.1.1:443 google.com:443 IP in IPv6 format with port: [2607:f8b0:400a:806:200]:80

The PCAP (Packet Capture or TCP Dump) command to capture network traffic. This allows admins to troubleshoot connectivity between an App Connector and Public Service Edge for Private Access (ZPA), or between an App Connector and applications. A maximum of one PCAP command per session is allowed. The maximum PCAP file size for a single session is 1 GB, while the maximum size of the individual PCAP files is 100 MB (e.g., if the PCAP capture is 350 MB, then three files are downloaded at 100 MB each, and then one file is downloaded at 50 MB). After the files are downloaded on the host machine, you can merge the files for analysis. After the PCAP session is complete, you can download the session output. To download the session output of the PCAP: Expand the PCAP session in the table. Click the App Connector or Private Service Edge for Private Access. The Session Output window appears. In the Session Output window, click the Download icon.

Examples of valid arguments: Interfaces: eth0 (optional) Application: jira.corp.com (optional) 10.1.1.1 (optional) IP in IPv4 and IPv6 formats: [2607:f8b0:400a:806:200] and [2607:f8b0:400a:806:200]:80 FQDN: Fully resolvable by the device as done by tcpdump. The maximum allowed characters is 51. IP with port supported: 1.1.1.1:80 FQDN with port: abc.com:80

The command to restart the VPN Service Edge or Network Connector process. Canceling a restart command that is in a Processing state is not supported. Restart commands cannot be run at the same time as a DNS lookup command or another restart command.

The command to restart the VPN Service Edge or Network Connector. Canceling a restart command that is in a Processing state is not supported. Restart commands cannot be run at the same time as a DNS lookup command or another restart command.
The command to start the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) for the selected VPN Service Edge or Network Connector.
The command to stop the BGP for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) feature.
The command to restart the BGP for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) feature.
The command to fetch the service status of the BGP for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) feature.
The command to reload the BGP configuration for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) feature.
The command to display all the routes or routes for a target network seen by the BGP service for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) feature.
Argument is optional. If not provided, target all is considered. Examples when using the argument to target a specific network: 10.10.10.0/24 10.10.10.1
Any valid IPv4 address with an optional CIDR range
The command to display all the interfaces or a specific target interface, seen by the BGP service for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) feature.
Argument is optional. If not provided, interface all is considered. Examples when using the argument to target a specific interface: eth0 vpn_vrf1
The command to display all routes, or routes for a specific target network, learned through the BGP service.
Argument is optional. If not provided, interface all is considered. Examples when using the argument to target a specific network: 10.10.10.0/24 10.10.10.1
Any valid IPv4 address with an optional CIDR range

The command to display all BGP neighbors, or a specific target neighbor, configured on the device. It provides information about the status, connection details, and prefixes exchanged with the neighbor.
Argument is optional. If not provided, interface all is considered. Examples when using the argument to target a specific peer: 240.0.0.1 240.0.0.2
Any valid IPv4 address with an optional CIDR range
The command to display a summary of BGP sessions, including connection state, uptime, and prefixes advertised, for monitoring BGP peers.
The command to reset all BGP sessions, or a specific peer BGP session, forcing a BGP reconnection.
Argument is optional. If not provided, interface all is considered. Examples when using the argument to target a specific peer: 240.0.0.1 240.0.0.2
Any valid IPv4 address with an optional CIDR range
The command to display the currently running BGP configuration for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) feature.
The command to display the last generated BGP configuration that failed to apply to the BGP service.
The command to display the last generated configuration of the BGP service.
The command to trigger the BGP config validation of the selected config mode (Generated or Override) and provide the validation output.
The command to trigger the BGP config validation and provide the config status of BGP for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) feature.
The command to trigger the BGP config validation based on current config mode and provide the detailed validation output.
The command to fetch the logs of the BGP service.
Argument 'No of Lines' option available in UI. Example 2000 5000

The command to fetch service logs or full system logs for an App Connector, Private Service Edge, or Private Cloud Controller to help troubleshoot and diagnose issues. In general, logs are compressed into an LZ4-formatted file (e.g., admin-probe-journalctl-<uuid>.lz4). The compressed file is then uploaded to an AWS S3 bucket for storage. In the following instances, logs skip compression: If the log file size is below 4 KB (e.g., logs collected over a very short interval). If the service is unavailable when the log is fetched. When compression is skipped, the log file is uploaded in its raw uncompressed format as downloaded_file.log. To download and decompress the log files: Expand the JOURNALCTL session in the table. Click the Download icon. Decompress the log file using an open-source LZ4 tool.

blocks.item: Targets: Enter the destination FQDN or IP address of the session. Separate multiple hostnames with a comma (,) and ports with a colon (:) (e.g., test.com, example.com:80, example.com:443, 10.1.1.1:8080).

Duration: Enter the duration for running the command. The minimum duration is 30 seconds, and the maximum duration is 5 minutes. If no value is entered, the default duration is 1 minute. This field appears only when a PCAP command is selected.
Interface: Enter a network interface name to limit the PCAP command to capture packets on a particular interface (e.g., eth0, eth1, eno). This field appears only when a PCAP command is selected.

Force: Select Enabled if you want the VPN diagnostic session to be activated during the selected time range. Select Disabled if you want the VPN session to be inactive. Disabled is selected by default. This field appears only when a RELOAD BGP CONFIG command is selected.

Configuration Mode: Select Generated to generate the commands. Select Override to override the commands. Override is selected by default. This field only appears if the CONFIG VALIDATE command is selected.
Number of Lines: Enter the number of command lines you want to set for this VPN diagnostic session. This field only appears if the GET LOGS command is selected.
Max Log Lines: Enter the maximum number of log lines to return. This setting has a default of 1,000 and a maximum value of 100,000. This field appears only when a JOURNALCTL command is selected.
Log Type: Select whether to return Service Logs or Full System Logs. This field appears only when the JOURNALCTL command is selected.

Time Range: Select the time range that you want the commands for the VPN session to run. This field only appears if the GET LOGS or JOURNALCTL command is selected. For JOURNALCTL, the maximum date and time is 4 hours from the current date and time.
Click Save.
